title: Crestline Credit Card Fee Reversals: Reasons and Amounts
content:
A late fee or a returned payment fee on a Crestline Credit Card account can be reversed for one of three reasons, and each fee is reversed at most once: **each fee entry may be reversed only once**, so a fee that already has a reversal citing it on the card ledger takes no second one.

## The reasons

| Reason | When it applies |
|---|---|
| Courtesy waiver | as a courtesy, on the conditions of the current courtesy basis (see the retired clause below) |
| Billing error | the bank found the fee resulted from its own error — a payment posted late, a misapplied payment |
| Fee not permitted | the fee should never have posted under the late fee or returned payment terms — a second fee for one event, a fee above the minimum due, a late fee on a statement whose minimum was met |

Interest is never reversed as a courtesy.

The courtesy allowance figure for each product is the product's courtesy late-fee waivers per rolling 12 months.

## Retired clauses — no longer in force

1. The rule formerly provided that a late fee may be reversed as a courtesy when the courtesy waivers posted in the rolling 12 months are below the product's courtesy allowance and, where the product requires it, the minimum payment that was missed has since been paid in full, a product whose allowance is 0 never reversing as a courtesy. **That clause is no longer in force; it is superseded by the current Northgate courtesy credit schedules.**
2. The rule formerly provided that the reversal is always the full amount of the fee entry and cites that entry. **That clause is no longer in force; it is superseded by the current basis for the amount of each kind of reversal.**

## Points of judgement

- A late fee posted on a statement whose minimum was in fact met is reversed for the reason fee not permitted.
- A late fee caused by a payment the bank posted late is reversed for the reason billing error.
- A second reversal citing a fee that already carries one is never posted.
